# OpenSeal

> Open-source (Apache-2.0) electronic-signature platform: send PDFs for signature, sign in the browser, seal with PAdES, and verify offline. Self-hostable with Docker Compose. Pre-release; designed to support ESIGN and eIDAS simple and advanced electronic signatures, not certified.

## Site

- [Brand and attribution | OpenSeal](https://seal.casualoffice.org/brand.html): OpenSeal logos to download, how to credit OpenSeal with Powered by OpenSeal, what the Apache-2.0 licence requires, and ready-made snippets.
- [Changelog | OpenSeal](https://seal.casualoffice.org/changelog.html): What changed in OpenSeal, by date.
- [Download and deploy | OpenSeal](https://seal.casualoffice.org/download.html): Ways to run OpenSeal v0.1.0, the first signed pre-release: the Docker Compose stack, the web app in demo mode, the openseal command line and the offline verifier.
- [OpenSeal: open-source e-signatures](https://seal.casualoffice.org/): OpenSeal is an Apache-2.0 signing and verification engine you embed (a Rust engine, a WebAssembly verifier, an API and SDK), with a complete e-signature web app built on it: send, sign, self-host, and verify every sealed PDF offline.
- [Roadmap | OpenSeal](https://seal.casualoffice.org/roadmap.html): What OpenSeal has built, what is in progress, Release 1, and the slices that follow.
- [Security policy | OpenSeal](https://seal.casualoffice.org/security.html): How to report a vulnerability in OpenSeal privately, what to include, what counts as critical, and which versions are supported.
- [Verify a sealed PDF | OpenSeal](https://seal.casualoffice.org/verify.html): Check a sealed PDF in your browser with OpenSeal's verifier compiled to WebAssembly: integrity, certificate trust, timestamp and revisions. The file is not uploaded.

- [Architecture overview | OpenSeal](https://seal.casualoffice.org/docs/architecture.html): OpenSeal's shape: a deterministic Rust engine for PDFs, seals and evidence, hosted by a server of record with a worker and a key daemon, and a web app on the public API.
- [Configuration reference | OpenSeal](https://seal.casualoffice.org/docs/configuration.html): Every environment variable of the OpenSeal server, worker and key daemon, and of the production profile: default, whether it is required, whether it is a secret, and what it does.
- [Contributing | OpenSeal](https://seal.casualoffice.org/docs/contributing.html): How to build, test and contribute to OpenSeal: the toolchain, the tests, the clean-room rule, commit conventions and where the plan lives.
- [Deploy with Docker Compose | OpenSeal](https://seal.casualoffice.org/docs/deploy-compose.html): Run OpenSeal on one machine with Docker Compose for evaluation: prerequisites, step-by-step commands, the first administrator, checking it works, and stopping or removing it.
- [Production deployment | OpenSeal](https://seal.casualoffice.org/docs/deploy-production.html): Deploy OpenSeal with the hardened production profile, step by step: host, DNS and TLS, secrets, the seal key in an HSM, timestamps, email, database and storage, signed images, backups, upgrades, monitoring, rotations and the production checklist.
- [FAQ | OpenSeal](https://seal.casualoffice.org/docs/faq.html): Frequently asked questions about OpenSeal: status, legal standing, licensing and commercial use, verification, keys, the API, and how it relates to DocuSign, SignNow and AGPL projects.
- [Sending your first envelope | OpenSeal](https://seal.casualoffice.org/docs/first-envelope.html): Upload a PDF, add recipients in routing order, place fields in the document-first editor, review and send an OpenSeal envelope.
- [Getting started | OpenSeal](https://seal.casualoffice.org/docs/getting-started.html): Run the whole OpenSeal stack on your machine with Docker Compose, create the first administrator, and send a test envelope.
- [Documentation | OpenSeal](https://seal.casualoffice.org/docs/index.html): OpenSeal documentation: run it, send and sign, verify, administer, integrate with the API and webhooks, and how the evidence model works.
- [Security and evidence model | OpenSeal](https://seal.casualoffice.org/docs/security.html): How OpenSeal protects a completed agreement: PAdES seals, trusted timestamps, the hash-chained audit trail, key custody in keyd, hostile-PDF handling, tenancy, and what is still to be reviewed.
- [Deployment overview | OpenSeal](https://seal.casualoffice.org/docs/self-hosting.html): How OpenSeal runs on your own infrastructure: its services, the evaluation stack and the hardened production profile, and which guide to follow.
- [Signing | OpenSeal](https://seal.casualoffice.org/docs/signing.html): What a signer sees in OpenSeal: the emailed link, access code, consent to electronic records, the guided path through fields, adopting a signature, review and finish.
- [Templates | OpenSeal](https://seal.casualoffice.org/docs/templates.html): Save documents, roles, fields and the email message once as an OpenSeal template, then send envelopes from it by filling in the people.
- [Troubleshooting | OpenSeal](https://seal.casualoffice.org/docs/troubleshooting.html): Common OpenSeal deployment failures and how to fix them: ports, services that will not start, keyd unreachable or refusing, timestamp authorities, email, envelopes stuck completing, and what the logs show.
- [Verifying a document | OpenSeal](https://seal.casualoffice.org/docs/verifying.html): Check an OpenSeal sealed PDF in the browser, offline, with the openseal command line, or with independent PAdES validators such as pyHanko and EU DSS.
- [Webhooks | OpenSeal](https://seal.casualoffice.org/docs/webhooks.html): OpenSeal webhooks: subscribing, event types, the payload, Standard Webhooks signatures, verifying them, retries and SSRF protection.
